eras.name: Return of Chinese Rule & the White Terror

events.title: Penghu 1 jawbone found in the strait
events.description: Partial jawbone (Penghu 1) found in Taiwan Strait channel suggests a previously unknown species of *Homo* inhabited the area when sea levels were ~140m lower and the strait was a land bridge

events.title: Oldest evidence of modern human presence on Taiwan
events.description: Oldest evidence of modern human presence on Taiwan: bone fragments and a tooth found at Zuojhen District

events.title: Changbin culture (Paleolithic chipped-pebble tools) found in Taitung
events.description: Changbin culture (Paleolithic chipped-pebble tools) found in Taitung; same culture at Eluanbi on the southern tip

events.title: Slash-and-burn farming at Sun Moon Lake
events.description: Evidence of slash-and-burn agriculture at Sun Moon Lake (pollen/spore analysis)

events.title: The Taiwan Strait forms
events.description: Sea levels rise at the start of the Holocene, forming the Taiwan Strait and cutting Taiwan off from the Asian mainland

events.title: Liangdao Man skeleton found on Liang Island (Matsu archipelago)
events.description: Liangdao Man skeleton found on Liang Island (Matsu archipelago)

events.title: Dapenkeng culture appears
events.description: Neolithic Dapenkeng culture appears abruptly and spreads around the coast; characterised by corded-ware pottery, polished stone adzes, rice and millet cultivation. Believed to be ancestors of today's Taiwanese aborigines, speaking early Austronesian languages

events.title: The Austronesian expansion begins in Taiwan
events.description: Some Dapenkeng descendants migrate from Taiwan to Southeast Asia and across the Pacific/Indian Oceans, making Taiwan the origin point of the Austronesian language family (Malayo-Polynesian is just one branch; all other branches are found only on Taiwan)

events.title: Wu dynasty troops raid Yizhou
events.description: Sun Quan, emperor of the Wu dynasty (Three Kingdoms period), sends troops to an island called Yizhou (possibly Taiwan). They take several thousand captives and return to China; the island is subsequently deemed "barbarian territory" and not worth China's attention

events.title: Local iron smelting begins
events.description: Wrought iron being produced locally using bloomeries, technology possibly introduced from the Philippines

events.title: Chinese fishermen settled on the Penghu Islands near Taiwan
events.description: Chinese fishermen settled on the Penghu Islands near Taiwan. "Bisheye" raiders (Taiwanese people related to the Bisaya of the Philippines) land on Penghu and plunder Chinese fields; Song dynasty sends soldiers and begins regular patrols

events.title: Kublai Khan's envoys mistake Taiwan for Ryukyu
events.description: Yuan dynasty emperor Kublai Khan sends officials to demand loyalty; they end up in Taiwan, mistake it for Ryukyu. Three soldiers are killed; the delegation retreats

events.title: Wang Dayuan writes the first description of Taiwan
events.description: Wang Dayuan visits Taiwan and provides the first detailed written description of the island, noting the presence of Chinese trade pottery but no Chinese settlers (many on Penghu, however)

events.title: The Ming navy at its height
events.description: Ming navy at its pinnacle with over 3,500 vessels, ~2,700 of which are warships stationed along the Chinese coastline

events.title: Taiwan used as a base by Japanese and Chinese merchants and pirates
events.description: Taiwan used as a base by Japanese and Chinese merchants and pirates; increasing numbers of Chinese fishermen, traders, and pirates visit the southwestern coast

events.title: Chinese from Fujian begin settling in southwestern Taiwan
events.description: Chinese from Fujian begin settling in southwestern Taiwan. Ming officials start issuing licences for trade in northern Taiwan (1593), acknowledging already-existing illegal trade

events.title: Portuguese maps name it Ilha Formosa
events.description: Portuguese sailors note Taiwan on their maps as *Ilha Formosa* ("beautiful island")

events.title: Portuguese castaways spend 45 days ashore
events.description: Portuguese shipwreck survivors spend 45 days on Taiwan battling malaria and aborigines

events.title: Chen Di writes the Dongfanji
events.description: Chen Di visits Taiwan on an anti-pirate expedition; writes *Dongfanji* ("An Account of the Eastern Barbarians"), one of the earliest detailed accounts of Taiwan's native peoples. Notes substantial Chinese settlers already living alongside the indigenous population

events.title: Sui expeditions to Liuqiu
events.description: Emperor Yang of the Sui sends three expeditions to a place the records call Liuqiu, which may be Taiwan or may be the Ryukyus. Nobody has settled which.

events.title: The Dutch find Chinese already settled
events.description: When the Dutch arrive, they find ~1,500-2,000 Chinese visitors and residents in two villages (one of which would become Tainan), plus a Chinese community living in an aboriginal village speaking a creole language

events.title: Fort Zeelandia built at Tayowan
events.description: Dutch East India Company (VOC) builds Fort Zeelandia on the islet of Tayowan off the southwest coast, after being driven from Penghu by Ming authorities. This becomes their main base

events.title: Li Tan's pirate fleet based on Taiwan
events.description: Li Tan ("Captain China") oversees a fleet of pirate ships while based in Taiwan

events.title: The Dutch found Sakam
events.description: Dutch buy land from the Sinkan village and build the town of Sakam for Dutch and Chinese merchants

events.title: Spanish settle at Keelung
events.description: Spanish establish a settlement at Santísima Trinidad in northeastern Taiwan (modern Keelung), building Fort San Salvador, as a counter to Dutch presence

events.title: Spanish build Fort Santo Domingo at Tamsui
events.description: Spanish build Fort Santo Domingo at Tamsui. Mattau and Soulang warriors kill 60 Dutch musketeers in an ambush

events.title: Zheng Zhilong beats the Dutch fleet off Quanzhou
events.description: Zheng Zhilong (Koxinga's father) defeats Dutch fleet in sea battle near Quanzhou; Dutch subsequently reconcile with Zheng, who arranges more Chinese trade in Taiwan

events.title: Dutch defeat Mattau and Baccluan; pacify multiple aboriginal villages
events.description: Dutch defeat Mattau and Baccluan; pacify multiple aboriginal villages. Dutch and allies massacre inhabitants of Liuqiu Island (sealing ~300 in caves, killing with poisonous fumes; population of 1,100 removed, men enslaved, women and children distributed)

events.title: Favorolang kills three Chinese
events.description: Favorolang (largest aboriginal village north of Mattau) kills three Chinese - beginning of years of conflict

events.title: Dutch build Fort Provintia on the main island's harbour shore
events.description: Dutch build Fort Provintia on the main island's harbour shore

events.title: The VOC pays Chinese settlers to come
events.description: VOC encourages mass Chinese migration to Taiwan; advertises economic benefits, even pays them to move. Thousands arrive as rice and sugar planters

events.title: The Dutch take Keelung from Spain
events.description: Dutch seize Spanish fortress at Keelung; Spanish and Filipino garrisons disperse or retreat to the Philippines. Dutch now control both north and south

events.title: Zheng Zhilong defects and Koxinga takes up the Ming cause
events.description: Zheng Zhilong (Koxinga's father) defects to the Manchu Qing; is captured and taken to Beijing in chains. His son Koxinga (Cheng Cheng-kung / Zheng Chenggong) burns his scholar's robes and takes up the Ming loyalist cause

events.title: Koxinga builds his fleet and army
events.description: Koxinga rebuilds his father's pirate fleet and army; establishes a major Ming outpost along China's south coast in Fujian. At his peak: ~50,000 cavalry, 70,000 infantry, 10,000 elite "iron men," and a fleet of over 3,000 junks

events.title: Dutch estimate ~50,000 natives in the western plains
events.description: Dutch estimate ~50,000 natives in the western plains; administer ~315 tribal villages with a total population of ~68,600

events.title: The Guo Huaiyi rebellion
events.description: A Chinese farmer leads an army of peasants against the Dutch over oppressive taxation. It is put down with about four thousand Chinese killed, and the rural labour force never recovers.

events.title: The Dutch legacy
events.description: The Dutch leave behind a romanised script for the Formosan languages, Christianity, a unified tax system, schools and the ho-ko system of mutual responsibility. Every later ruler keeps them.

events.title: Koxinga's army routed at Nanjing
events.description: Koxinga besieges Nanjing with ~170,000 men; on the verge of victory, he throws a birthday celebration and his drunken army is routed by a Manchu cavalry night sortie. Retreats to Xiamen with only 400 battered junks

events.title: Koxinga invades Taiwan
events.description: Koxinga launches invasion of Taiwan with 25,000 soldiers on 400 war junks from Kinmen; receives ecstatic welcome from Chinese settlers on the island

events.title: Dutch warship *Hector* explodes and sinks in battle
events.description: Dutch warship *Hector* explodes and sinks in battle. Fort Provintia surrenders to Koxinga

events.title: Koxinga renames the Dutch forts
events.description: Fort Zeelandia becomes Anping and Fort Provintia becomes Chikan. He establishes one prefecture and two counties.

events.title: Koxinga's son Zheng Jing rules
events.description: Koxinga's son Zheng Jing rules. Establishes Ming-style administration with Six Ministries, Confucian Shrine, Imperial Academy, and civil service examinations. Dispatches teachers to aboriginal tribes; expansion of Chinese settlements comes at the expense of aboriginal land, causing rebellions. Chinese population more than doubles

events.title: After a nine-month siege, Fort Zeelandia surrenders
events.description: After a nine-month siege, Fort Zeelandia surrenders. Dutch colonial rule ends (though they hold out at Keelung until 1668)

events.title: Koxinga dies at age 37
events.description: Koxinga dies at age 37. Chinese nationalists in the 20th century invoke him for his patriotism and loyalty against the Qing and Western influence

events.title: Zheng Jing joins the Revolt of the Three Feudatories
events.description: Zheng Jing joins the Revolt of the Three Feudatories; recaptures territory on the mainland coast but is eventually forced back to Taiwan after a series of defeats

events.title: Zheng Keshuang murders his brother
events.description: Zheng Jing dies; political turmoil as his son Zheng Keshuang murders his brother. Multiple followers defect to the Qing

events.title: Cultivated land triples under the Zheng
events.description: By the end of Zheng rule the cultivated area has tripled since the Dutch era and sugar exports exceed Dutch figures. The government extracts over thirty per cent more silver a year than the Dutch did in 1655.

events.title: A state of constant rebellion
events.description: Taiwan described as in "a state of constant rebellion." Most rebellions caused by Han settler disputes, not aboriginal resistance. Major uprisings every few years; ethnic tensions between Hoklo and Hakka settlers add to instability

events.title: Western plains hold 2.5 million Chinese settlers
events.description: The western plains are fully developed and hold some 2.5 million Chinese inhabitants. The mountains remain largely autonomous aboriginal territory.

events.title: The Qing fleet takes Penghu
events.description: Shi Lang leads Qing fleet of 238 ships and 21,000+ men against Penghu; decisive naval battle in which ~12,000 Zheng forces perish. Penghu falls

events.title: Zheng Keshuang surrenders; shaves his head in Manchu style
events.description: Zheng Keshuang surrenders; shaves his head in Manchu style. Kingdom of Tungning ends

events.title: Kangxi annexes Taiwan as a prefecture
events.description: After debate (some officials advocated abandoning Taiwan entirely), Kangxi Emperor accepts Shi Lang's proposal to annex Taiwan. Established as Taiwan Prefecture, a sub-unit of Fujian Province

events.title: Migration banned, and the illegal traffic that followed
events.description: The Qing forbid mainlanders from moving to Taiwan and send most of them back, holding the official population at 50,000. Illegal migrants number tens of thousands a year by 1711.

events.title: Migrants barred from bringing their families
events.description: Migrants are barred from bringing their families, to ensure they would return. It produces the idiom about having a Tangshan father and no Tangshan mother: the overwhelmingly male migrants married locally, including aboriginal women.

events.title: The Zhu Yigui rebellion
events.description: An anti-Qing uprising sparked by increased taxation takes all of Qing-held Taiwan in under two weeks. The Qing fleet crushes it and Zhu is executed.

events.title: Boundary stelae divide settler from aboriginal land
events.description: Boundary markers (54 stelae) erected to segregate Chinese settlers from aboriginal territory. Rebuilt in 1750, 1760, 1784, and 1790 as encroachment continued regardless

events.title: The Lin Shuangwen rebellion
events.description: Tiandihui members break their jailed comrades out, and the rising draws in new arrivals who could not find land. Lin attacks Changhua and kills two thousand civilians before sixty thousand Qing troops suppress him.

events.title: British suggest seizing Taiwan during the First Opium War
events.description: British suggest seizing Taiwan during the First Opium War. In 1841 British try to scale heights around Keelung harbour three times but fail. Shipwreck survivors (over 130 from the *Nerbudda*, 54 from the *Ann*) are executed in Tainan in 1842

events.title: The Rover shipwreck
events.description: American barque *Rover* shipwrecks off southern Taiwan; captain and crew killed by Paiwan aborigines. US Consul Le Gendre negotiates with aboriginal chief Tanketok

events.title: Ryukyuan sailors shipwreck on southeastern Taiwan
events.description: Ryukyuan sailors shipwreck on southeastern Taiwan; 54 killed by aborigines (the Mudan Incident)

events.title: Japan's punitive expedition to southern Taiwan
events.description: Japan invades southern Taiwan using the Mudan Incident as pretext; 3,600 Japanese troops occupy indigenous territory for six months. 561 Japanese die (mostly of illness). Qing pays indemnity; Japan withdraws but gains recognition of Ryukyu as its vassal

events.title: Ban on entering Taiwan lifted
events.description: Ban on entering Taiwan lifted. Imperial commissioner Shen Baozhen recommends subjugating aborigines and populating their territory with Chinese to prevent further Japanese encroachment

events.title: The French invade northern Taiwan
events.description: In the Keelung campaign the French take the port but cannot advance beyond its perimeter, blockade the island, and eventually withdraw under agreement.

events.title: Taiwan elevated to a full province (previously a prefecture of Fujian)
events.description: Taiwan elevated to a full province (previously a prefecture of Fujian). Governor Liu Mingchuan launches modernisation: telegraph lines, railway (Keelung-Taipei-Hsinchu), electric lighting, modern weaponry, steamship service

events.title: Liu's campaigns against the aborigines fail
events.description: Liu launches 40+ military campaigns against aborigines with 17,500 soldiers; a third of the invasion force killed or disabled. Campaigns largely unsuccessful despite modern weapons (Gatling guns, mortars, land mines). Liu declares victory in a memorandum to Beijing but in reality achieves little

events.title: The railway plagued by corruption and sabotage
events.description: Corruption, incompetence and sabotage dog the line. Soldiers burn the surveying pegs for firewood, officers divert routes for bribes, and two tunnel faces drilled from opposite ends meet fourteen feet apart. The Japanese later rebuild much of it from scratch.

events.title: Liu resigns due to political opposition and recurring malaria
events.description: Liu resigns due to political opposition and recurring malaria; modernisation efforts largely cease under his weak successor

events.title: The Taiwan Republic declared in Taipei
events.description: The Taiwan Republic is formally declared in Taipei, its declaration saying the people of Taiwan are determined to die rather than be subdued by the Japanese. The tiger flag on a blue ground is still a potent symbol for independence advocates.

events.title: T'ang inaugurated as president
events.description: T'ang is inaugurated as president of a republic that calls itself suzerain to the Qing: semi-independent, acknowledging only a general overlordship from Beijing.

events.title: The Imperial Guard lands at Aoli
events.description: The Japanese Imperial Guard comes ashore at Aoli, southeast of Keelung.

events.title: Keelung falls after a day's fighting
events.description: Keelung falls after a day's hard fighting. The defence is shambolic: militia under independent gentry warlords refuse to coordinate.

events.title: President T'ang flees by ship
events.description: President T'ang flees on a German passenger ship. Shore batteries fire on it as it steams out of Tamsui harbour.

events.title: Ch'iu Feng-chia leaves for the mainland
events.description: Ch'iu Feng-chia also leaves for the mainland, and never returns to Taiwan.

events.title: Japanese troops enter Taipei unopposed
events.description: The Japanese enter Taipei unopposed after Guangdong soldiers go on a looting rampage that kills at least five hundred people. Taipei's merchants invite the Japanese in to restore order.

events.title: Resistance stiffens in the south
events.description: Resistance stiffens in the south. Black Flag Liu Yung-fu forms a temporary government in Tainan and issues its own money and postage stamps.

events.title: Tainan is handed over without a fight
events.description: Tainan is surrendered without fighting after Liu flees in disguise aboard a British ship.

events.title: No power recognises the republic
events.description: Not one of the European powers or the United States ever recognised the Taiwan Republic: **Between 200,000 and 300,000 people flee Taiwan** in 1895. From 1895 to 1897, ~6,400 sell their property and leave

events.title: What the republic left behind
events.description: The republic lasted five months, but it told the Taiwanese their fate was in their own hands: when their future was in the balance, both China and the great powers deserted them.

events.title: Five months of war, then seven years of partisans
events.description: Five months of sustained warfare after the invasion, followed by partisan attacks until 1902. At least 12,000 "bandit-rebels" killed (in addition to 6,000-14,000 killed in the initial resistance war)

events.title: Arrests and uprisings under Japanese rule
events.description: At least 8,200 Taiwanese arrested each year for alleged attempts to overthrow Japanese rule. 19 major uprisings during the entire period of Japanese rule, including 2 attempts to take Taipei

events.title: Treaty of Shimonoseki cedes Taiwan to Japan
events.description: Having lost the First Sino-Japanese War, the Qing cede Taiwan and Penghu to Japan in perpetuity. The loss becomes a rallying point for Chinese nationalism.

events.title: Gentry press the governor to declare independence
events.description: Civic leaders led by Hakka gentry member Ch'iu Feng-chia pressure Governor T'ang Ching-sung to declare independence

events.title: 6,000 Taiwanese slaughtered in the Yunlin Massacre
events.description: 6,000 Taiwanese slaughtered in the Yunlin Massacre

events.title: Goto Shimpei appointed chief civil administrator
events.description: Goto Shimpei appointed chief civil administrator. Implements "biological colonial management" - work with Taiwanese customs first, then gradually reshape them. Creates omnipresent police force (~12,000 officers + 5,000 in aboriginal areas) and revives ho-ko (mutual responsibility) system. Taiwan becomes a thorough police state

events.title: What Japanese rule builds
events.description: Unified weights and measures, centralised banking, schooling, a rail network joining north and south, dam-fed irrigation covering more than half the farmland, ports and a health system.

events.title: Food output quadruples, sugar fifteenfold
events.description: Food production increases fourfold and sugar cane fifteenfold between 1895 and 1925. Taiwan becomes a major food basket for the Japanese economy.

events.title: Life expectancy reaches sixty
events.description: Average lifespan reaches sixty years by 1945, up sharply from where it stood under the Qing.

events.title: Most Taiwanese felt their lives had improved
events.description: Most Taiwanese felt their lives had improved: under Japanese rule compared to previous Chinese rule, despite the repression

events.title: Harsher policy towards the aborigines
events.description: Government implements harsher policies toward aborigines: expands guard lines, restricts living space. Sakuma Samata launches five-year plan using landmines and electrified fences

events.title: The Beipu uprising
events.description: Hakka and Saisiyat insurgents kill fifty-seven Japanese. A hundred Hakka men and boys are killed in reprisal.

events.title: The army moves into the mountains
events.description: Army invades mountainous areas; by 1915 many aboriginal villages destroyed. By 1903, indigenous rebellions had already killed 1,900 Japanese

events.title: Luo Fuxing (Tongmenghui member) plans a rebellion
events.description: Luo Fuxing (Tongmenghui member) plans a rebellion; over 1,000 Taiwanese executed by Japanese police

events.title: The Tapani Incident
events.description: Yu Qingfang's religious group defies Japanese authority. Some 1,413 are captured and Yu and two hundred followers executed. Military police lure further militants out with a pardon and then shoot them in a field; oral tradition puts the toll at five or six thousand.

events.title: Aborigines relocated onto reserve land
events.description: Aborigines relocated; allotted 3 hectares of reserve land each, later reduced. Given less than half the originally promised land, or one-eighth of ancestral lands

events.title: The first petition for self-determination
events.description: Lin Hsien-tang and 178 Taiwanese file a petition seeking self-determination; rejected. Petitions continue annually

events.title: The Taiwanese Cultural Association founded
events.description: Chiang Wei-shui founds the Taiwanese Cultural Association (TCA); promotes vernacular Chinese language. "Taiwan is Taiwan people's Taiwan" becomes common position for all anti-Japanese groups

events.title: Taiwan People's News founded in Tokyo
events.description: TCA co-founds Taiwan People's News (published in Tokyo, shipped to Taiwan, subjected to censorship). 99 Alliance members arrested for attempting to set up a parliament

events.title: TCA splits
events.description: TCA splits; factions include the Taiwanese People's Party and a subsidiary of the Taiwanese Communist Party (the only group advocating outright independence)

events.title: The Musha uprising
events.description: The last major aboriginal rebellion. Seediq warriors under Mona Rudao attack police stations and a school, killing about 134 Japanese. The fighting ends in December when the Seediq leaders take their own lives.

events.title: The cost of the aboriginal wars
events.description: Across the conflicts with aboriginal peoples, roughly 4,422 civilians died, about 2,660 military were killed and some 4,160 wounded.

events.title: TPP terminated by authorities
events.description: TPP terminated by authorities. Chiang Wei-shui dies

events.title: War with China and the kominka project
events.description: Full-scale war with China; kōminka (imperial Japanisation) project launched. Chinese language removed from newspapers and education; Taiwan's history erased from curriculum

events.title: Over 207,000 Taiwanese employed by Japanese military
events.description: Over 207,000 Taiwanese employed by Japanese military. ~50,000 go missing or die; 21 executed for war crimes

events.title: Taiwan as a base for the southward advance
events.description: The island is used for the invasion of Guangdong in 1938 and the occupation of Hainan in 1939, then to launch the southward advance after Pearl Harbor. It is the base for naval and air attacks on Luzon and rear staging for Myanmar.

events.title: The name-changing campaign
events.description: Taiwanese are pressed to adopt Japanese names. Only seven per cent have done so by the end of the war.

events.title: Taiwanese women forced into the comfort women system
events.description: Between one and two thousand Taiwanese women are forced into the system, and aboriginal women serve the Japanese military in the mountain regions. More than half are minors, some as young as fourteen.

events.title: Taiwan's real GDP per capita peaks at $1,522
events.description: Taiwan's real GDP per capita peaks at $1,522; declines to $693 by 1944 due to wartime destruction

events.title: War damage across the island
events.description: Forty per cent of the railways are unusable, more than two hundred factories have been bombed and three of the four power stations destroyed. About 350,000 Japanese civilians are living on the island.

events.title: Taiwan bombed in US air raids
events.description: Taiwan bombed in US air raids; estimated 16,000-30,000 civilians killed

events.era_name: Return of Chinese Rule & the White Terror
events.title: Chen Yi's administration and the looting
events.description: Chen Yi establishes a military administration staffed entirely by mainlanders and his own relatives. Looting begins at every level: soldiers carry off stolen bicycles on their backs because they cannot ride them, officers ship Japanese stores to the mainland to sell, and Chen's circle seize about ninety per cent of the economy through monopolies.

events.era_name: Return of Chinese Rule & the White Terror
events.title: Prices spiral and the rice crop halves
events.description: Food prices rise more than 21,000 points between November 1945 and January 1947. The rice crop falls to half its 1930s level, and bubonic plague and cholera become endemic again as the quinine stores are sold to the mainland.

events.era_name: Return of Chinese Rule & the White Terror
events.title: The dogs have gone and the pigs have arrived
events.description: Wall posters around the island read "the dogs have gone and the pigs have arrived", and "at least the Japanese dogs protected property".

events.era_name: Return of Chinese Rule & the White Terror
events.title: Emperor Hirohito announces Japan's surrender
events.description: Emperor Hirohito announces Japan's surrender. Taiwanese wait eagerly for liberation. Nothing happens for weeks - Japanese maintain order, police continue patrols

events.era_name: Return of Chinese Rule & the White Terror
events.title: Chen Yi receives the Japanese surrender
events.description: General Chen Yi (appointed by Chiang Kai-shek) arrives and receives Japanese surrender. Proclaims Taiwan reincorporated into China. Allies object: the legal resolution awaits a formal peace treaty; KMT merely administers Taiwan on behalf of the Allies

events.era_name: Return of Chinese Rule & the White Terror
events.title: Troops fire on the crowd in Taipei
events.description: Several thousand people march on the commission offices and then the governor's office. Soldiers fire a machine gun into the crowd, the uprising spreads island-wide within two days, and martial law is declared.

events.era_name: Return of Chinese Rule & the White Terror
events.title: The settlement committee's 32 demands
events.description: Civic leaders form a settlement committee and present thirty-two demands, including an end to military rule, autonomy for the province, free elections and the release of political prisoners. Chen rejects them.

events.era_name: Return of Chinese Rule & the White Terror
events.title: Kuomintang reinforcements land at Keelung
events.description: Ten thousand Kuomintang reinforcements land at Keelung and three thousand at Kaohsiung. The troops begin a campaign of indiscriminate shooting, rape and bayoneting.

events.era_name: Return of Chinese Rule & the White Terror
events.title: The hunt for Taiwanese leaders
events.description: Government forces systematically hunt anyone counted a leader of Taiwanese society: lawyers, businessmen, newspaper editors, members of the settlement committee. Many are tortured and mutilated before being killed and their bodies left in the streets, and about a hundred middle school students are executed arbitrarily. The KMT's own records put the dead at at least 28,000.

events.era_name: Return of Chinese Rule & the White Terror
events.title: Chen Yi recalled and promoted
events.description: Chen Yi is recalled in March and promoted to governor of Zhejiang. In 1949 he is caught trying to defect to the Communists, and is shot in Taiwan in June 1950; the news sparks a day of celebration across the island.

events.era_name: Return of Chinese Rule & the White Terror
events.title: The cigarette seller beaten in Taipei
events.description: Widow Lin Chiang-mai, selling cigarettes in a Taipei park, is accosted by Monopoly Commission agents. She is struck with a pistol butt; an agent fires into the crowd, killing one man

events.era_name: Return of Chinese Rule & the White Terror
events.title: Communists win the Chinese Civil War
events.description: Communists win the Chinese Civil War. Soviet Union supported communists; US supported the KMT

events.era_name: Return of Chinese Rule & the White Terror
events.title: Chiang's plan: regroup, then retake the mainland
events.description: Regroup on Taiwan, then return to the mainland. The slogan is to prepare for one year, counter-attack in two, sweep out the enemy in three and succeed within five.

events.era_name: Return of Chinese Rule & the White Terror
events.title: Mainlanders dominate government and the civil service
events.description: Mainlanders hold the government and the civil service outright. The KMT administration is exclusively mainlander, is not commercially minded, and is deeply unpopular.

events.era_name: Return of Chinese Rule & the White Terror
events.title: Martial law from 1947 to 1987
events.description: Martial law runs from 1947 to 1987, the White Terror. The Taiwan Garrison Command's secret police hunt dissidents, opposition parties are banned, and the island is governed as a one-party state with token elections at district level only.

events.era_name: Return of Chinese Rule & the White Terror
events.title: Land reform caps rents at 37.5% of crop value
events.description: Rents are capped at 37.5 per cent of crop value, the government sells confiscated Japanese farmland in family-sized lots, and landlords must sell their excess holdings. At least two million Taiwanese become landowners, farm incomes double, and productivity is up by half by 1963. It creates the equity base for the industrial revolution that follows.

events.era_name: Return of Chinese Rule & the White Terror
events.title: Chiang Kai-shek formally moves the ROC capital to Taipei
events.description: Chiang Kai-shek formally moves the ROC capital to Taipei. ~2 million mainlanders flood to Taiwan (1.2 million in December alone), including 600,000 surviving KMT army members. Only ~6 million local Taiwanese on the island at this point

events.era_name: Return of Chinese Rule & the White Terror
events.title: US aid: $1.5 billion economic, $2.4 billion military
events.description: Taiwan receives $1.5 billion in US economic aid and $2.4 billion in military aid. US advisers help frame land reform, infrastructure, and industrial policy. Aid is ~$100 million/year through the 1950s, representing a third of all capital investment

events.era_name: Return of Chinese Rule & the White Terror
events.title: Truman writes off Taiwan
events.description: President Truman announces US will have no further involvement in the Chinese civil war. Washington writes off Taiwan

events.era_name: Return of Chinese Rule & the White Terror
events.title: Korean War breaks out
events.description: Korean War breaks out. Two days later Truman orders the 7th Fleet to patrol the Taiwan Strait (both to prevent Chinese invasion of Taiwan AND to prevent Chiang from invading the mainland). Taiwan is suddenly "the unsinkable aircraft carrier"

events.era_name: Return of Chinese Rule & the White Terror
events.title: San Francisco leaves Taiwan's status unspecified
events.description: Japanese Peace Treaty signed in San Francisco: Japan formally relinquishes Taiwan but does not specify a recipient. The legal status of Taiwan remains ambiguous

events.era_name: Return of Chinese Rule & the White Terror
events.title: Inflation finally curbed
events.description: Inflation finally curbed by trimming money supply and high-interest savings deposits

events.era_name: Return of Chinese Rule & the White Terror
events.title: US and ROC sign a defence treaty
events.description: US and ROC sign a defence treaty. US prohibits Kuomintang from unilateral offensive action against the mainland

events.era_name: Return of Chinese Rule & the White Terror
events.title: Communist shelling of Kinmen and Mazu
events.description: Communist shelling of Kinmen and Mazu. US pressures Chiang to abandon some offshore islands; he refuses most

events.era_name: Return of Chinese Rule & the White Terror
events.title: The light industrial revolution
events.description: Taiwan becomes an export-driven economy that the world calls a miracle. Enterprising farmers turned entrepreneurs use their land equity as collateral for bank loans.

events.era_name: Return of Chinese Rule & the White Terror
events.title: A staging post for the Vietnam War
events.description: Taiwan is used as a staging point for American bombing raids on North Vietnam and as a rest and recreation centre for troops.

events.era_name: Return of Chinese Rule & the White Terror
events.title: US shuts off economic aid tap
events.description: US shuts off economic aid tap; Taiwan is a going concern

events.era_name: Return of Chinese Rule & the White Terror
events.title: Defence takes twelve per cent of GDP
events.description: Military spending runs as high as twelve per cent of GDP, sustained by the constant threat from the mainland.

events.era_name: Return of Chinese Rule & the White Terror
events.title: Chiang orders a nuclear weapons programme
events.description: Chiang orders advanced nuclear weapons program using a Canadian research reactor; later agrees to dismantle it under US pressure

events.title: US calls Taiwan's status undetermined
events.description: The American official position is that Taiwan's status is undetermined. The PRC replaces the ROC at the United Nations.

events.title: Nixon visits China
events.description: In the Shanghai Communique the United States acknowledges the Chinese position that Taiwan is part of China, without endorsing it.

events.title: Chiang Ching-kuo begins to loosen control
events.description: Chiang Ching-kuo, formerly head of the feared secret police, recognises that foreign support requires reform. He gradually loosens political controls and begins the Taiwanisation of the regime.

events.title: Chiang Kai-shek dies
events.description: Chiang Kai-shek dies. Succeeded by Yen Chia-kan as president; son Chiang Ching-kuo becomes KMT chairman and president in 1978

events.title: US formally recognises Beijing (PRC) and derecognises Taipei (ROC)
events.description: US formally recognises Beijing (PRC) and derecognises Taipei (ROC). Congress passes Taiwan Relations Act, committing US to provide Taiwan with defensive weapons and maintain capacity to resist coercion

events.title: The Kaohsiung Incident
events.description: Police attack pro-democracy demonstrators, and the arrests and trials of opposition leaders that follow galvanise Taiwanese civil society.

events.title: The DPP founded as the first opposition party
events.description: Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) established as the first opposition party. Chiang Ching-kuo decides against dissolving it

events.title: Martial law lifted after 40 years
events.description: Martial law lifted after 40 years. Family visits to mainland China allowed

events.title: Chiang Ching-kuo dies
events.description: Chiang Ching-kuo dies; succeeded by native Taiwanese Lee Teng-hui as president - first non-mainlander to hold the post

events.title: First direct presidential election
events.description: First direct presidential election. Lee Teng-hui wins. China fires missiles into the sea and conducts mock invasion exercises; US responds by sending two aircraft carrier battle groups to the area

events.title: Chen pledges not to declare independence
events.description: Chen promises not to declare independence unless China attacks, not to change the name Republic of China, and not to hold a referendum on status. It is more conciliatory than Lee Teng-hui in some respects, but Beijing refuses to engage.

events.title: Beijing misreads the KMT
events.description: Beijing courts the KMT, believing mainlander conservatives will negotiate unification. It misunderstands the nature of Taiwan's political transformation.

events.title: Chen Shui-bian wins and ends KMT rule
events.description: DPP candidate Chen Shui-bian wins presidency with 39% of the vote (KMT vote split between Lien Chan and James Soong). Ends 55 years of KMT rule. Beijing's dream ticket falls apart because Lien and Soong harbour deep personal dislikes

events.title: The DPP takes the legislature
events.description: DPP becomes the largest party in the legislature (with support from Lee Teng-hui's new Taiwan Solidarity Union), though still without a majority. Chen begins "de-Sinicisation" policies: promoting Minnan dialect, "rectification of names," teaching Taiwanese history separately from mainland context

events.title: US reconnaissance plane forced down by Chinese jets
events.description: US reconnaissance plane forced down by Chinese jets. Bush approves major arms sale to Taiwan; says the US would do "whatever it took" to defend Taiwan

events.title: 9/11 attacks shift US priorities
events.description: 9/11 attacks shift US priorities. Beijing grasps the opportunity: aligns with Washington on anti-terrorism, gains leverage on Taiwan issue. Chen fails to appreciate the changed dynamic

events.title: Chen re-elected after an assassination attempt
events.description: Chen narrowly re-elected (assassination attempt the day before the election). China deploys ~500 missiles aimed at Taiwan (growing to ~700 by mid-2005)

events.title: The Pentagon on China's submarine force
events.description: Pentagon admits Chinese submarine force already a deterrent to swift US intervention in a Taiwan crisis

events.title: Ma Ying-jeou wins the presidency with 58.5%
events.description: KMT's Ma Ying-jeou wins presidency (58.5% of the vote) on a platform of friendlier relations with China and economic reforms. Chen Shui-bian later prosecuted for corruption

events.title: Ma re-elected
events.description: Ma re-elected; KMT retains legislative majority

events.title: The Sunflower Movement
events.description: Students occupy parliament in protest at the KMT pushing a trade agreement with China through without proper debate. It changes the mood of the electorate.

events.title: DPP's Tsai Ing-wen wins presidency with 56% of the vote
events.description: DPP's Tsai Ing-wen wins presidency with 56% of the vote. DPP wins outright majority in the legislature - first time a non-KMT party achieves this

events.title: Local elections set the DPP back
events.description: A major setback for the DPP. The KMT wins Kaohsiung, a DPP stronghold for twenty years, and Tsai resigns as party leader.

events.title: Taiwan becomes the first country in Asia to legalise same-sex marriage
events.description: Taiwan becomes the first country in Asia to legalise same-sex marriage

events.title: Tsai re-elected
events.description: Tsai re-elected; DPP wins 61 of 113 legislative seats

events.title: Ukraine shifts Taiwanese views of the threat
events.description: Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine changes Taiwanese public perceptions of the Chinese threat. Accelerates military reform, new weapons acquisitions, higher military spending, and investment in civil defence

events.title: Nancy Pelosi visits Taiwan
events.description: Nancy Pelosi visits Taiwan. PLA conducts military exercises around Taiwan, including missile launches that overfly the island

events.title: William Lai Ching-te (DPP) wins presidential election
events.description: William Lai Ching-te (DPP) wins presidential election. No party wins a legislative majority for the first time since 2004: DPP 51 seats, KMT 52 seats, Taiwan People's Party (TPP) 8 seats
